title: Young players coming up
summary: Young players should get road experience; he predicts a not-yet-20 player will be one of the big ones.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Oh, there are lots of good guys around. Even who are willing to go out and maybe travel a little and stuff.

Yeah. I mean they -- I don't mind it if -- if a young guy can do it -- It's OK for a young guy to do it you know. He's got his health and everything. And then he can get experience which you do need to be a band musician.
Yeah. You have a fairly young musicians still coming up who are growing up in the (inaudible).
Oh yeah, there's one in particular -- a musician that I know of that he'll probably some day
be a -- one of the big ones and that's (PHONETIC). He's -- I don't think he's 20 yet you know. But he plays like mad -- he's beautiful.
Yeah, yeah, he -- I was surprised how much he had improved when I --
I hadn't heard him in a couple of years now --
Yeah, he was (inaudible) but he kept on at it and now he sounds good -- great.
So even though -- you know -- the music has moved off on a lot of different tangents, there's still like a basic core that will remain that young musicians will come up and they'll still play --
I'm not talking about Dixieland -- I'm talking about jazz really.
